sentences.text: Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the complainant has lodged a complaint before the Police Station against the present applicant alleging that on 11.07.2017 the applicant took her to his government quarter as he is a government servant and has committed sexual intercourse with her.

She has also stated in the complaint that the accused has promised her to marry and on the pretext of marriage he Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1790 was making physical relationship with her and all of a sudden without informing her he was transferred to Raipur.
It is also the case of the prosecution that the complainant visited Raipur when she asked him to marry then he has refused and threatened her and thereafter she has lodged the report.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is falsely implicated for the offence as complainant has demanded money and when he refused to give money then she has lodged the complaint.

He would further submit that the applicant is a major lady and is well aware of the consequences of physical relationship, as such, it is a consensual act and he would pray for releasing the applicant on anticipatory bail.
To substantiate his submission he has referred to the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Jude Lobo Vs. State, NCT of Delhi decided on 29.03.2021.

entities.text: Jude Lobo Vs. State, NCT of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State oppose the submission and would submit that in the statement recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C. the victim has clearly alleged that the applicant has made physical relationship with her for the last 4-5 years on the pretext of marriage.
He would further submit that the applicant has assured her to marry and on his assurance she has visited Raipur for marriage, later on he refused to marry.
Thus, prima facie involvement of the applicant is reflected and would pray for rejection of anticipatory bail.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the case diary.

6. Considering the age of the victim and statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 wherein the victim has stated that the accused has also given Rs. 8 lakhs to her and out of this amount she Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1790 has purchased the land in the name of her mother and also considering the fact that the victim is a major lady, I am of the view, that it is a fit case where the applicant should be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

7. Accordingly, M.Cr.C.(A) is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with the aforesaid offence, he shall be released on bail by the officer arresting him on executing a personal bond in sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.

The Applicant shall also abide by the following conditions :
(i) that the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation before the concerned police officer as and when required;
(ii) that the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat undue influence to the prosecution witnesses.
